CircularEconomy.label: Circular economy
CircularEconomy.title: From vehicle identification to waste collection and treatment.
CircularEconomy.intro: We develop the applications manufacturers and recyclers use to manage take-back operations: identifying a vehicle, assessing a battery, preparing a pickup, negotiating a price, and generating and tracking documents.
CircularEconomy.positioning: Automakers, repair shops, battery holders, collectors, and recyclers: tools to declare, organize, and track each take-back.

CircularEconomy.proofNote: The features presented come from several projects developed for automotive manufacturers and recycling operators. They illustrate our work; scope and rules are adapted to each organization.

CircularEconomy.dossiersTitle: Three ways to explore our work in detail.
CircularEconomy.dossiersIntro: From fields completed by the declarant to partner integrations, each guide explains the data, rules, documents, and actions involved.
CircularEconomy.audienceTitle: What problem do you need to solve?

audiences.question: What is stopping us from preparing this pickup?
audiences.answer: Battery record, packaging, selected packages, collector, and delivery site: all the necessary information is brought together before the packing list is created.

audiences.question: How can owners and service providers work on the same records?
audiences.answer: A declaration workflow for the network, management interfaces for internal teams, and data exchanges with treatment facilities. Access rules reflect each party’s responsibilities.

audiences.question: What treatment price and logistics cost were agreed?
audiences.answer: Each proposal retains its price components, author, date, and status. The history shows both the terms discussed and those accepted.

audiences.question: Does the record contain the right code, documents, and required signatures?
audiences.answer: EWC codes, battery diagnostics, documents, and waste tracking form statuses are handled within the workflow. Application controls highlight required items and incomplete steps.

audiences.question: What information should be exchanged with existing systems?
audiences.answer: Battery data, status changes, and accepted offers can flow to partner systems through APIs and notifications. Each business object and its access rights are considered when defining the integration.

CircularEconomy.scopeTitle: A focused module or a complete application.

scopeItems.title: Extend an existing tool
scopeItems.text: Does your logistics software work well, but declarations still arrive by email? The project can focus on collecting the information and passing it to that system.

scopeItems.title: Improve a workflow that has become limiting
scopeItems.text: Does your network already use an application? We identify the data, rules, and integrations that must be preserved before extending or replacing the relevant component.

scopeItems.title: Build an end-to-end service
scopeItems.text: Are you setting up a new take-back operation? We can develop the network portal, administration tools, and partner integrations you need.

faqs.question: Is this an off-the-shelf software product?
faqs.answer: We design and develop custom applications. The examples show features we have already built; together, we define which ones meet your needs, which rules to adapt, and which systems to connect.

faqs.question: Do we have to replace our existing tools (ERP, transport, MES, billing, etc.)?
faqs.answer: The first step is to determine what your existing tools already cover. An integration or complementary module may be enough. We review the integration options with your IT teams before agreeing on the scope.

faqs.question: Does the application guarantee regulatory compliance?
faqs.answer: It implements the controls and document exchanges defined for the project. Waste classification, transport rules, and applicable obligations must be validated by the responsible specialists. An EWC code or a Trackdéchets connection alone does not guarantee compliance.

faqs.question: Do you only work with vehicles and batteries?
faqs.answer: These are the sectors illustrated by the projects shown here. For another activity, we examine the similarities and differences in products or materials, stakeholders, documents, transactions, and existing tools. The deciding factor is whether our experience applies to the operations you need to support.

faqs.question: Where does AI fit?
faqs.answer: When a need involves reading documents, extracting information, or assisting with assessments, we can explore an AI component. Not all the features in these guides depend on AI: API-based identification, input rules, and status exchanges already address concrete needs.

CircularEconomy.ctaTitle: Define the scope of a real workflow
CircularEconomy.ctaText: Show us a real workflow, the people involved, and the tools already in place.

dossiers.label: End-of-life vehicles
dossiers.title: Identify the vehicle. Complete the record. Organize take-back.
dossiers.summary: License plate or VIN, retrieved specifications, administrative documents, and interfaces for the take-back network.
dossiers.description: An individual or a repair shop starts by declaring a vehicle. Beyond that form, teams need reliable information, prepared documents, and a request they can pass to the parties responsible for collection. Here are the features we have developed to connect these steps.
dossiers.context: Project example: a vehicle take-back platform with individual and professional workflows connected to an existing management system.

sections.title: Start with a plate or VIN, not an empty record.
sections.navLabel: Vehicle data enrichment by plate / VIN
sections.situation: Enrich a vehicle record from a license plate or VIN: retrieve the available make, model, and specifications from an identification service.
actions: The declarant provides the registration country and the available identifier: a license plate or VIN, the vehicle identification number.
The application queries an identification service and populates the record with the returned specifications.
The user is prompted to complete any required fields that remain empty. Manual entry is available when data cannot be retrieved.
sections.rule: The identification method and required fields vary by country. The integration does not assume that every lookup returns a complete record.
sections.result: A structured vehicle record populated with the available specifications and completed with any missing information.

sections.title: Move the request and its administrative record forward together.
sections.situation: The workflow collects the declarant’s documents, generates the transfer and destruction documents required for the French operations covered, and sends them to the signers.
actions: The workflow brings together the information and documents needed to handle the request.
The team finds these items in the vehicle record rather than in separate exchanges.
The generation and electronic signing of transfer and destruction documents are integrated into the process for the relevant French operations.
sections.rule: Document content and signature steps depend on the country and procedure. The project uses the applicable documents and defines the expected signatories.
sections.result: The request, supporting documents, and signature tracking are linked to the relevant vehicle.

sections.title: Give the network a shared operational tool.
sections.situation: Separate interfaces let individuals and repair shops declare vehicles, authorized treatment facilities track handovers, and program teams monitor network progress.
actions: Separate workflows support individual and professional requests.
Management interfaces let teams and partners track vehicles and handling steps.
Connections to the existing system carry the information needed from declaration and collection through dismantling and final tracking.
sections.rule: The public portal and professional tool serve different purposes. Screens and access rights need to reflect that separation.
sections.result: Vehicle-level tracking and interfaces suited to the people declaring, handling and managing operations.

dossiers.label: Batteries, collection & recovery
dossiers.title: A battery to handle, along with its specifications, constraints, and take-back terms.
dossiers.summary: EWC code, condition and diagnostics, packing lists, treatment and transport prices, receipt, and treatment tracking.
dossiers.description: A battery is more than a reference and a pickup address. Its type, condition, documents, and agreed terms affect how it is handled. We have developed the modules below for recycling and second-life projects.
dossiers.context: Examples from several applications developed for an automotive manufacturer and a battery recycler. The modules are presented together to explain the operations they support.

sections.title: Identify the battery and record its waste code.
sections.navLabel: Battery identification, VIN / BIN and reference data
sections.situation: The declaration combines VIN or BIN identifiers with reference characteristics: model, dimensions, and weight. The holder adds condition, charge, state of health, EWC and UN codes, supporting documents, and photos.
actions: The declaration links the battery to its type and holder information.
The workflow suggests an EWC (European Waste Catalogue) code using the existing declaration or reference battery type.
The declarant can select or correct the code. It is saved in the record, and any changes can be viewed in the history.
sections.rule: Prefilled information comes from reference data. It does not replace validation of the waste classification by the responsible stakeholders.
sections.result: A fully characterized battery record ready for collection, transport, and traceability.

sections.title: Capture battery condition before collection.
sections.situation: The declarant records the battery’s condition and attaches diagnostics, photos, and a checklist. The interface displays the ADR transport information associated with the selected condition.
actions: The declarant records battery condition and attaches the diagnostic and checklist documents required by the workflow.
ADR transport information associated with the selected condition is shown in the interface.
Overview photos are requested, along with a serial-number photo when required based on the declarant and the readability of the identifier.
sections.rule: Required documents depend on context. Transport and packaging rules are defined with the responsible specialists; the portal does not infer them from a photograph.
sections.result: A record bringing together declared condition, photos and documents needed to assess handling.

sections.title: Build a consistent packing list.
sections.situation: The user groups packages from several declarations into a packing list. The application checks collector and destination-site compatibility to prepare a shared shipment.
actions: Users review declarations with their owner, collector, delivery site, chemistry, packaging, and status.
They select the packages to include in the packing list.
In the workflow we developed, the selection controls prevent incompatible delivery sites or collectors from being included in the same group.
sections.rule: This grouping check is an explicit business rule. For your organization, we define the criteria that allow or prevent packages from being shipped together.
sections.result: A packing list linked to declarations, packaging, palletization and the planned transport.

sections.title: Separate the treatment price from the logistics cost.
sections.situation: Providers propose separate treatment and logistics prices, with a currency and comment. Each offer is retained with its author, date, and acceptance or rejection.
actions: A proposal includes the treatment price, logistics cost, currency, and an optional comment.
Each successive proposal is retained with its author, date, and acceptance or rejection status.
Service providers can also manage proposals through an API. Notifications can inform their systems when a proposal is created or accepted.
sections.rule: This example covers price negotiations for batteries and pickup groups. A trading arrangement involving multiple purchase and resale contracts would need to be scoped separately.
sections.result: Proposed and agreed terms remain available with the record, without searching an email chain for the latest agreement.

sections.title: Connect collection, receipt, and treatment.
sections.situation: The application tracks ready-for-pickup, collected, received, and treated stages. Receipt records the date and operator; Trackdéchets exchanges update the waste tracking form in the relevant workflows.
actions: Statuses distinguish batteries that are ready for pickup, collected, received, or treated.
In a workflow connected to Trackdéchets, the receipt step records a date and the recipient’s name, then updates the linked waste tracking form and declaration.
Partners can be notified of status changes to update their own tracking.
sections.rule: Physical and document tracking are linked but remain distinct. The workflow shows the current stage and any actions still required.
sections.result: A declaration tracked after departure from the holder’s site, with the associated steps and documents.
data: Linked waste tracking form, where applicable

dossiers.label: Documents & integrations
dossiers.title: Keep information and documents connected to operations.
dossiers.summary: EWC, ADR, Trackdéchets waste tracking forms, signatures, and API exchanges: what the applications handle and where your systems fit.
dossiers.description: Operations often involve several applications. The business record needs to retain useful references, track document stages, and send events to partners. Here are some of the integrations and controls we have developed.
dossiers.context: Examples from vehicle and battery projects. Document obligations and integration capabilities must be checked for each country, activity and system involved.

sections.title: EWC and ADR: separate information, separate purposes.
sections.situation: Waste classification codes and transport information need to be recorded in the right place. Grouping them under a compliance label does not explain what the tool actually does.
actions: The EWC code is linked to the declaration and can be suggested from the reference battery type.
Battery condition is recorded separately with the required diagnostic documents.
The interface displays the ADR information defined for that condition. Teams define input rules, supporting documents, and required approvals.
sections.rule: The application organizes data and applies defined rules. It does not automatically turn an EWC code into authorization for transport or treatment.
sections.result: Distinct, accessible information that helps qualified stakeholders review the record.

sections.title: Track the waste tracking form with the declaration.
sections.situation: The application creates and updates waste tracking forms through Trackdéchets, monitors producer and collector signatures, and then transmits receipt and treatment information.
actions: The application creates or updates a BSD through Trackdéchets and stores its identifier with the declaration.
It checks the form’s status and distinguishes a missing producer signature from a missing collector signature.
The workflow can make receipt conditional on these signatures, then transmit receipt and treatment information.
sections.rule: A blocked step should explain why and who needs to resolve it. This describes a control in the developed workflow, not a universal legal rule.
sections.result: The form and declaration remain linked; the user sees document status and required actions.

sections.title: Link signatures to the right record.
sections.situation: A document sent for signature should remain connected to the vehicle or operation that generated it.
actions: In the relevant vehicle workflows, transfer and destruction documents are generated within the process.
The DocuSign electronic signature service is integrated into the workflow.
The business record provides access to the documents and signature progress.
sections.rule: Signatories, documents, and signature timing are defined by the procedure. The project also accounts for incomplete steps.
sections.result: The request, prepared documents, and signature status remain connected.

sections.title: Exchange business objects, not just files.
sections.situation: APIs and notifications exchange battery data, price offers, and status changes with providers’ systems. Imports and exports complement these exchanges according to the tools in place.
actions: A service provider API supports battery data imports and exports as well as price proposals.
Outgoing notifications report specific events: a battery assigned, ready for pickup, received or processed; an offer created or accepted.
Access is authenticated and limited to the partner’s scope. Interfaces and exchange formats are defined for the relevant operations.
sections.rule: Integrating with your ERP or logistics software requires an assessment of the available data, direction of exchange, access rights, and error handling. We do not assume that a universal connector exists.
sections.result: A partner can update tracking from its system and receive events relevant to its operations.

hero_section.description: We build tools that connect your data, SaaS platforms, and internal systems to make your operations faster, more reliable, and more automated. AI is not bolted on as an afterthought; it is designed into your day-to-day processes as a core capability.

fdti_section.subtitle: Your data and tools are the starting point. Code and AI where they matter. Operations that are more streamlined, reliable, and automated.
fdti_section.content_1:
We start with the work your teams actually do: processing documents, retrieving information, preparing decisions, streamlining coordination, and automating tasks.

  • Identify the steps where AI delivers tangible value
  • Connect the right sources: databases, SaaS platforms, files, APIs, and internal tools
  • Design a robust, secure system your teams can use every day
fdti_section.content_2:
We deliver the right type of solution for each need: a copilot, an assisted workflow, an API, an administration interface, or a complete business application.

  • AI copilots: search, summarization, decision support, assisted writing
  • Process automation: document processing, assessment, coordination, alerts, reporting
  • Business applications: portals, dashboards, administration interfaces, secure APIs, and internal tools

Architecture, security, deployment, and monitoring are part of the product. We define access, hosting, data flows, and controls with each client based on their specific context.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.content:
Legal framework – compliance with the GDPR and French law

FDTI Consulting processes personal data in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of April 27, 2016, on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data (hereinafter the GDPR), and with French Law No. 78-17 of January 6, 1978, on information technology, data files, and civil liberties.


The General Data Protection Regulation took effect on May 25, 2018. Organizations that process data must ensure the highest possible level of data protection at all times and be able to demonstrate their compliance through documentation.


Given the nature of its work, FDTI Consulting may need to process personal data collected and processed by its clients. The following provisions define FDTI Consulting's internal processing rules and are intended to ensure that personal data is handled in accordance with the GDPR.


FDTI Consulting considers the protection of personal data fundamental to all its activities. It seeks to anonymize all data it processes as early as possible and works to prevent its disclosure outside the applicable legal frameworks.

Governance

Data processed by FDTI never leaves the European Union and is not subject to any jurisdiction outside the European Union.


Our hosting provider, OVH France, is based in France and hosts our services in France. It is therefore not subject to the CLOUD Act.

Personal data processing

Except in specific cases, FDTI Consulting does not need personal data to perform its services. FDTI Consulting therefore asks its clients not to send it personal data. If FDTI Consulting receives personal data unexpectedly, it will delete the data immediately and notify the sender.


Some personal data may be useful for identification purposes. In such cases, FDTI Consulting will ask the data provider to pseudonymize the data and will assist with the pseudonymization process.

If the sender lacks the technical or human resources to perform this pseudonymization in its own environment, FDTI Consulting will handle it. Only one person within FDTI Consulting will have access to the personal data for the purpose of pseudonymizing it and sharing only the pseudonymized data within FDTI Consulting.


All personal data used in our work is stored securely and processed in accordance with the consent provided by the data subjects. The data is permanently deleted once the studies and processing required for our projects have been completed.

page_tags.title: Data, AI, and business software projects | FDTI
page_tags.description: Explore systems deployed by FDTI, from AI for commercial courts and circular economy platforms to retail data and public lighting monitoring and modeling.

use_case_list.title: AI platform for commercial courts
use_case_list.challenge: A software vendor for commercial court clerks wanted to embed AI directly into its platform to improve the speed and accuracy of specific time-consuming clerical tasks.
use_case_list.approach: A modular architecture organized around specialized AI use cases and tailored LLMs. An on-premises FastAPI AI stack is fully integrated with the existing platform through an API and is also available to other users through a secure API. The portal is built with TypeScript and SvelteKit.
use_case_list.impact: AI pre-analysis runs in parallel with business workflows. The first use case processes around 40 billion tokens per year, delivering substantial time savings while meeting judicial confidentiality requirements.
details: Critical use cases covered: case summaries, filing validation, and automated extraction from sensitive documents using LLMs and OCR.
Deployment inside the client's VPN with fine-grained monitoring and contractual SLAs.
Self-service portal to generate API keys, track usage, and troubleshoot calls.
Re-annotation loops to improve models plus full audit tooling.
Adoption program with training, operational guides, and dedicated support.
TypeScript/SvelteKit frontend delivering a frictionless experience alongside legacy tools.

use_case_list.title: End-of-life vehicle management platform
use_case_list.challenge: Following the creation of Valorauto, a joint venture between Stellantis and Galloo, the circular economy platform needed to modernize its existing system to manage B2B and B2C take-back of end-of-life vehicles and track each vehicle from collection at the owner's location through dismantling.
use_case_list.approach: Development of the Valorauto portal, with interfaces for declarations, administration, and vehicle tracking across stakeholders. Business workflows and Azure Functions APIs deployed on the client's Azure infrastructure (MSSQL databases and Azure Service Bus) orchestrate an existing .NET stack connecting owners and authorized treatment facilities.
use_case_list.impact: End-to-end traceability for the group's circular economy business, supporting a network of more than 5,000 partner companies and helping the manufacturer meet its Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) obligations.
details: End-to-end development of the platform, databases, and APIs.
Complete declaration workflow design for dealers, repair shops, and private owners.
Azure Functions APIs connecting the group's logistics, CRM, and finance systems.
API integration with the wider circular economy ecosystem (recyclers, owners, buyers, and producer responsibility organizations).
Real-time mapping of material flows and automatic generation of regulatory documents.
Multi-brand management: local rules, catalogs, and pricing by country.
Azure infrastructure sized to handle peaks in regulatory activity and audits.
Operational and regulatory dashboards consolidating B2B and B2C flows.
Personalized email notifications for every user (garages, dealers, private owners) at each workflow step.

use_case_list.title: Battery reuse marketplace
use_case_list.challenge: An automotive manufacturer needed a central tool to manage the collection, recycling, and resale of its batteries in collaboration with partners and buyers. The tool had to provide end-to-end process traceability to meet regulatory requirements as Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) systems were being established.
use_case_list.approach: A web marketplace connected to partner ERP systems that serves as both a logistics and matchmaking platform. It provides end-to-end traceability, automates flows to buyers or recyclers, and integrates price and terms negotiations with partners. The entire process can be managed through the portal or the API.
use_case_list.impact: Several thousand batteries are routed each month by hundreds of owners and service providers, with centralized reporting for authorities and an administration interface for the client's employees. The solution integrates seamlessly with the existing ecosystem.
details: End-to-end development of the platform, databases, and APIs.
Complete declaration workflow for end-of-life batteries, including automated generation of logistics documents.
API integrations with recyclers and producer responsibility organizations to track pickups, tests, certificates, and price proposals.
Buyer workspace to source batteries suitable for reuse and manage the transaction.
Quality and compliance scoring with shared SLAs.
One-click regulatory reporting exports.
Automated email notifications for partners and buyers across pickup, testing and resale steps.
Identity federation through Keycloak for group entities and external partners.

use_case_list.title: Operations platform for a battery recycler
use_case_list.challenge: A recycler needed a single tool for battery declarations, preliminary reviews, collection preparation, tracking documents, receipt, and treatment stages.
use_case_list.approach: Development of a business application connecting declarations, battery reference data, packing lists, grouping controls, Trackdéchets waste tracking forms, and receipt actions.
use_case_list.impact: Teams track each record from declaration through treatment, with explicit controls for collectors, destination sites, signatures, and document statuses.
details: Assessment of declarations based on battery chemistry, sub-chemistry, and type.
Packing lists that prevent incompatible collectors or destination sites from being grouped together.
Creation and updating of Trackdéchets waste tracking forms, with visibility into required signatures.
Receipt of declarations and treatment stages tracked in the same business record.
Interfaces suited to internal teams and collection partners.

use_case_list.title: Public lighting monitoring and modeling
use_case_list.challenge: A company specializing in public lighting management for municipalities and their service providers needed a single platform to manage public lighting, adjust schedules, detect anomalies, and plan maintenance.
use_case_list.approach: Development of a web application that serves as a management portal and provides analytical dashboards. The real-time stack combines AWS S3, DuckDB, and Parquet, with Shell/Cron pipelines, a FastAPI backend, and a TypeScript/SvelteKit interface.
use_case_list.impact: Network managers use the application every morning. Consumption and incident metrics update dynamically, with predictive maintenance and alerting deployed across more than 40 territories.
details: Continuous collection of lighting meter data with optimized S3 and Parquet storage.
Shell/Cron pipelines to refresh the cache.
DuckDB analytics delivering KPIs instantly across years of historical data, with dynamic visualizations of the results.
Management of mandates associated with data owners and users.
Alert dashboards for operators (failures, consumption, schedule anomalies).
Open REST API for connecting service provider and municipal systems.
Multi-tenant management with granular permissions and segmentation by operator.

use_case_list.title: AI analysis of social media campaigns
use_case_list.challenge: The NGO needed to compare environmental narratives on Facebook and Instagram to guide its communications spending.
use_case_list.approach: An LLM-based methodology uses ChatGPT and tailored prompts to score tone, topics, and perspectives. The results are correlated with Facebook and Instagram KPIs by audience type (age, country, and interests) and presented in comparative visualizations.
use_case_list.impact: Budgets were reallocated by country and platform, and the analysis framework was adopted internally.
details: Prompts capturing tone, stakeholders, topics, and emotions on Facebook and Instagram.
Automated pipeline: social media data → LLM → scoring of topics, tones, and perspectives by audience type.
Correlation with post performance to recommend priority themes.
Documented methodology replicable by local teams.
Training sessions to help teams interpret recommendations and adjust budgets.

use_case_list.title: Data hub & NLP
use_case_list.challenge: A leading consumer electronics company in France needed to centralize customer review data and scale its analysis using AI and dashboards.
use_case_list.approach: Airflow-to-BigQuery pipelines collect data via APIs from multiple providers and collection systems, supported by GCP governance and NLP models (Hugging Face, BERTopic, QA, and LLMs). Results are delivered through Tableau dashboards and distributed internally to the relevant teams.
use_case_list.impact: Customer service can instantly find classified topics and escalated alerts while tracking requests more accurately. The product team identifies and anticipates defects and logistics issues, while the legal team can better anticipate disputes.
details: Data collection from multiple APIs (mystery shopping, CRM, social media, and reviews), orchestrated by Airflow.
Cloud policies covering team segmentation, data localization, security, and best practices.
Analysis and classification pipeline with LLMs.
NLP pipelines for similarity, sentiment, and topic analysis across multiple languages.
Design and implementation of dashboards used daily by the Customer & Market insights team.
Documentation and training for data and business teams.
Automated insight exports to marketing business units and agencies.

use_case_list.title: Near real-time data warehouse
use_case_list.challenge: As part of an ERP migration, the client needed to move 98 high-volume, complex JSON business objects (stores, warehouses, users, receipts, inventory, and more) from Azure to Snowflake to feed Qlik in near real time.
use_case_list.approach: Hundreds of SQL and Scala queries were generated automatically from specifications to flatten complex objects. The system creates and feeds more than 150 tables and views updated in real time. Data is ingested from ADLS into Snowflake through Kafka and ADF, with orchestration handled by streams and tasks.
use_case_list.impact: BI teams receive minute-by-minute data feeds while the system processes millions of files each day. The organization transitioned to the new analytics system and then deprecated the legacy platform.
details: Automatic SQL generation from XML metadata to speed up deployments.
Incremental updates orchestrated by Snowflake Tasks with dedicated monitoring.
Custom Scala functions to denormalize nested JSON.
